title: The dashboard's sync writes to the board branch, never to the branch you are standing on
name: sync-branch
description: Root cause of f2592f9, which wiped development and was pushed to origin on 2026-09-24. The server's `sync` and `resolve` routes (packages/server/src/routes.ts:259 and :269) pass `baseOf(paths, branch)` as the board branch, and when no branch is given that is `currentBranch(paths.root)`. The dashboard's Sync button gives none. So `sync()` in packages/core/src/sync.ts runs `snapshot()` against `development`: it builds a tree that holds only `.sober/` records, commits it as a child of development's HEAD, and pushes it. The MCP `sync` tool (packages/mcp/src/tools/sync.ts) reads `config.value.board.branch` and is correct. Fix: both routes read the board branch from the config the same way the MCP tool does, and the request's `branch` field is dropped, or refused when it is not the configured board branch. Defense in depth in core: `sync()` and `resolveConflict()` refuse a branch that is the current HEAD's branch, or that is not the configured board branch, before any commit. Plumbing that commits a board-only tree must never be able to land on a code branch. Tests: a server route test where the working checkout sits on a code branch, sync is called with no branch, the code branch's HEAD and tree are unchanged, and the board branch gets the commit. A core test where `sync(paths, <current branch>)` throws and writes nothing.

brief.approach:
**Where it goes wrong.** In `packages/server/src/routes.ts`, the `sync` route (line 256) and the `resolve` route (line 262) pass `await baseOf(paths, branch)` as the board branch. With no `branch` in the body, which is exactly what the dashboard sends (`App.tsx:196` `op('sync', {})`, `App.tsx:506` `op('resolve', { record, choices })`), that becomes `currentBranch(paths.root)`, the code branch. `sync()` in `packages/core/src/sync.ts` then runs `snapshot()`. It commits a tree that holds only `.sober/` records as a child of that branch and pushes it. Every other caller already reads the configured branch: the MCP tool (`packages/mcp/src/tools/sync.ts:55`), the CLI (`packages/cli/src/resolve.ts:63,317`, `packages/cli/src/board.ts:72`, `hook.ts:175`) and the server's own `distance` route (routes.ts:376).

**1. Server: read the board branch from config, like `distance`.** In routes.ts, lift the body of `distance` that reads the config into one small local helper, `boardBranch(paths)`. It calls `readConfig(paths)`. If the config does not read, it throws the same `SoberError('no-board', …)` that `distance` throws. Otherwise it returns `config.value.board.branch`. `distance` uses the helper for its fallback. `sync` and `resolve` call it and drop the `branch` field from their `z.strictObject` bodies. No client sends that field, and a body that names a branch is exactly the hole, so the strict schema now refuses it. `baseOf` stays for the routes that really mean the code branch (accept, reject, review and the like).

**2. Core: the plumbing cannot land on a checked-out branch.** In `packages/core/src/sync.ts`, `sync()` and `resolveConflict()` compare `branch` with `await currentBranch(root)` (`packages/core/src/git.ts:83`) first, inside their `withLock` and before `createBoardBranch`/`snapshot`. If they are equal, they throw a `SoberError` that says: `<branch> is the branch checked out here, not a board branch — the board lives on <branch> named by board.branch in .sober/config.jsonc`. This guard catches any future caller that makes the same mistake, before anything is committed or pushed. It does not read the config itself: core's `sync` takes the branch as a parameter, and "never the checked-out branch" is the invariant the doc comment above `sync` already promises ("a sync in the middle of a code branch leaves that branch, its index and its HEAD exactly where they were"). A detached HEAD reads as `HEAD` from `currentBranch` and never equals a board branch name, so it passes.

**Tests.**
- `packages/core/src/sync.test.ts`: build a temp repo the way the file's existing tests do. Check out `main` with one code file committed and a board on disk. `sync(paths, 'main')` rejects. `main`'s HEAD sha and `git ls-tree main` are unchanged, and no `sober: board from` commit exists anywhere. The same holds for `resolveConflict(paths, 'main', …)`.
- `packages/server/src/routes.test.ts` (or `serve.test.ts` if the repo fixture is there): with the checkout on a code branch, `OPS.sync.run(paths, {})` leaves the code branch's HEAD unchanged, and the configured board branch (`sober-graph`) gains the `sober: board from …` commit. Also, `OPS.sync.accepts` refuses `{ branch: 'main' }`.
- The existing integration suites that call `sync(paths, BRANCH)` with `BRANCH = 'sober-graph'` (`test/integration/conflict.test.ts`, `board.test.ts`, `digest.test.ts`, `mcp.test.ts`) pass unchanged. They never sync the checked-out branch.

**Out of scope.** Repairing history (development was already restored in e246e39). The `accept` branch-delete bug is its own node (accept-branch-delete-287k).

acceptance.run: pnpm --filter @besober/core build && pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/sync.test.ts
acceptance.proves: core's sync and resolveConflict refuse the checked-out branch and leave its HEAD and tree untouched

acceptance.run: pnpm --filter @besober/core build && pnpm --filter @besober/server build && pnpm vitest run packages/server/src
acceptance.proves: the server's sync route commits to the configured board branch, never the checked-out one, and refuses a body that names a branch

acceptance.run: pnpm build && pnpm vitest run --project integration test/integration/conflict.test.ts test/integration/board.test.ts
acceptance.proves: real syncs and conflict resolution against sober-graph still work end to end
the changed route shapes typecheck against the dashboard's calls and pass biome
